question: Can an explicit shared-displacement budget force a valid time without reconstructing the complete allowed set?
status: FROZEN before calculation; known controls are development data, not held-out validation
candidate: For positive integer speeds and reduced anchor a/d with d<=n, nonzero anchor residues are already safe. In a fixed direction intersect their current safe laps and the collision speeds' first safe laps. Latest entry E=max(1/(n*v) for anchor colliders, default 0); earliest exit X=min((1-1/n)/v for colliders, and direction-specific remaining safe phase divided by v otherwise). X>E certifies a strict interior; X=E one valid instant; X<E refutes only this simultaneous first-safe-lap itinerary.
scope_limits: No new physical speed lists, phase changes, references, search or automatic resumption.
Keep the small-gcd result's original selected window distinct from a global witness at another time.
Compare with existing one-variable, directed-equality and adaptive-pair arguments; no novelty claim.
General sufficient proposition, finite reproduction and limitations remain separate.
verification: Exact fractions. Derive candidate solely from residues and speeds. Independently reconstruct first safe displacement bands through threshold-state sweeps, retaining isolated points. Check every certificate on all threshold cells and endpoints, and keep an entry/exit conflict for every failed itinerary.
